title: Interconnect Optimization for Timing and Power [IOTAP]
problem: Complex SOC CAD tools' multi-objective optimization algorithms leave residual sub-optimality in design outputs. End designs contain unidentified sub-optimal signal interconnect that could benefit from re-routing and parameter tuning.
motivation: Advancing analytics and AI enable automated sub-optimality detection and correction, offering last-mile improvements in timing and power that standard CAD tools miss due to tool heuristics and design space exploration limitations.
method: The approach automatically scans the signal interconnect (the wires connecting different parts of a chip) using a multi-variate cost function (a formula balancing multiple factors like speed and power consumption) to find routes that aren't optimally designed. For each poorly routed connection, the system recommends better track assignments (alternative routing paths) and incrementally re-routes the interconnect step-by-step, allowing the process to scale efficiently across large designs.
key_novelty: The core innovation is automatically detecting suboptimal signal routes in completed designs and recommending incremental re-routing improvements to gain timing and power efficiency, regardless of which tool originally created the design.
contributions: Multi-variate cost function for interconnect sub-optimality characterization
limitations: Abstract only; success rate of 60%+ indicates method works for majority but not all designs; power gains modest (0.53%) despite larger timing gains.
